AAPL.rationale: Apple's Q2 FY2026 results (reported April 30) show accelerating momentum: revenue of $111.2B (+17% YoY), EPS of $2.01 (+22% YoY), and gross margin expanding to 49.3% — all above consensus. Services revenue hit a new all-time high of $31B (+16% YoY), and the company guided June-quarter revenue growth of 14-17%, well ahead of the ~9.5% Street expectation. The installed base reached new all-time highs across all product categories. Operating cash flow of $28B+ in the quarter and a new $100B buyback authorization with a 4% dividend increase underscore capital return commitment. The shift away from a net-cash-neutral target signals greater flexibility. On valuation, the stock trades at ~34x trailing P/E, near the lower end of its 30-43x range over the past year, and P/B has compressed from 62x to ~46x. This is not cheap in absolute terms but is reasonable relative to Apple's own history given the reacceleration in growth. Key risks include the CEO transition (Tim Cook to John Ternus in September), regulatory/antitrust headwinds on App Store economics, China geopolitical exposure, and tariff cost headwinds (~$1.4B/quarter). The near-term catalyst is the strong Q2 print and above-consensus guidance, which should drive analyst estimate revisions upward. The capital-light AI strategy (partnering with Alphabet for Siri rather than building massive data centers) preserves cash flow while still participating in the AI upgrade cycle.
